title: SEO content brief
footer_left: SEO content brief template by Angel Phommachan

blocks.title: Reader and goal
fields: Reader
Who is this for? Specific enough to picture.
Marketers starting out who write their own blog posts
Goal
What should they know or be able to do when they finish?
Write a one-page brief before their next post

blocks.title: Search
blocks.hint: Free tools work: the Ahrefs Keyword Generator, Google's autocomplete, and the "People also ask" box.
fields: Main keyword
The phrase your reader types into Google. Add monthly searches and difficulty if your tool shows them.
seo content brief (500 searches a month, easy)
Related searches
Two or three other phrases or questions people search.
seo content brief template, content brief template
What searchers want
Search the main keyword. What kind of page shows up most: a how-to, a list, a review?
Step-by-step guides, most with a template

blocks.title: What already shows up on Google
blocks.hint: Open the top three results that aren't ads. Skim their headings and look for what they skip.
after: What it covers, and what it leaves out.

blocks.title: Your angle
fields: What's missing
What none of the top three do. Use section 03.
Every guide is written for agency teams, not people writing their own posts
What only you can add
A story, photo, result, or example from your own work.
My own filled-in brief and what I'd change
Your angle
The one idea your post adds, in one sentence.
A plain-language brief for people who write their own posts
Length
A range. Average the top three and divide by 3 for a starting point, not a rule.
900 to 1,200 words

blocks.title: Title and Google listing
blocks.hint: This is what people see in search results before they click.
fields: Page title
Main keyword near the start. About 60 characters or fewer so it isn't cut off.
How to Write an SEO Content Brief (With a Free Template)
Meta description
The short description under your title on Google. About 150 characters. Google may rewrite it.
How to write an SEO content brief in seven plain steps, what has changed in search and what hasn't, plus a free template you can download.
Web address (URL)
Short, lowercase, words separated by hyphens.
/blog/how-to-write-an-seo-content-brief

blocks.title: Ready to write?
blocks.body: You should be able to say the reader, the goal, and what's missing in one sentence each. If you can't, keep researching before you draft.

blocks.title: Outline
blocks.hint: Turn the questions people search into headings. Big questions become sections (H2), follow-up questions become subsections (H3). A rough word count for each keeps the length on track.

1: Main keyword in the first 100 words
8: Two or three questions from "People also ask"

blocks.title: Links, sources, and photos
blocks.hint: Link two or three of your own posts. Use competitors' pages for research, and link to neutral sources like the original report. Credit every photo.

blocks.title: Next step and proof
fields: Next step for the reader
The one thing they should do after reading (your call to action), plus the link.
Download the template
How you'll know it worked
One number to check 30 days after publishing.
Template downloads and Google ranking

blocks.title: Notes for the writer
blocks.hint: Skip this if you're writing it yourself, or use it to remember the rules you set.
fields: Voice
How it should sound.
Plain and friendly, first person
Must include
Required lines, disclaimers, product names, or terms.
A credit line for every photo
Avoid
Claims, words, or topics to leave out.
Any number I can't link to a source

blocks.title: Before you publish
items: Main keyword in the title, the first 100 words, and one section heading
Every number links to a source you opened
Two or three links to your other posts
Photos credited, each with a short description for screen readers (alt text)
Page title and meta description match section 05
The next step matches the goal in section 01
A reminder on your calendar to check your number in 30 days

example.title: Example: a filled-in brief
example.subtitle: The brief behind “Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?” on angelphommachan.com. Search numbers from Ahrefs, US. Section word counts are from the finished post.
rows: People starting out in marketing who want to see how two brands grow after one hit product
Understand the tradeoff between refreshing a best-seller and launching new products
owala vs stanley (1,800 searches a month, easy to rank for)
owala color drop (4,600), why is owala so popular (250), stanley marketing strategy
Shoppers comparing the bottles: every top result is a product test
No one compared the two brands’ marketing
My own side-by-side read of their products, ads, and blogs
New colors or new products: what each strategy costs and when it works
Average ÷ 3 ≈ 470 words; finished at about 1,480 to cover products, ads, and blogs
Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?
Owala sells the same FreeSip in a new color every month. Stanley is building bags, coolers, and soccer collections around the Quencher. What each costs.
Notice where each brand’s ads and links send you, then answer: refresh it or build something new?
Google ranking for “owala vs stanley” and time on page after 30 days
outline: Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?
Two bottles, two answers, plus a comparison table
How Stanley turned a work cup into a craze
Why Stanley is building past the Quencher
How Owala's Color Drops keep fans coming back
Is Owala more popular than Stanley?
How the bottles, ads, and blogs differ
Owala vs. Stanley: which strategy works?
What is an Owala Color Drop? Is Owala more popular than Stanley?
links: Liquid Death vs. Poppi, How the Utah Mammoth Got Its Name
Retail Dive, Fast Company, The Drum, Owala’s Color Drop FAQ, ASI (each opened and checked)
Brand photos from Stanley and Owala, each credited
note: One quote I planned to use was no longer on Owala’s site, so it came out before drafting. A classmate pointed out that the main growth number came from a search tool companies use to order branded gifts, so the post now says that plainly.
